param: ONE knob: the lensfun ptlens distortion model installed for the 24-70/4 S @ 70. A = incumbent (a=0.00350093 b=0.01453356 c=0.00043983, fitted 2026-07-17 on the retired arm rig, the model EVERY existing product was warped with). B = x86 re-fit (a=0.0033627 b=0.0149465 c=0.0005744, 887eb00, same frames, this rig's hugin-tools 2025.0.1). Everything else identical: same 54 frames (even stride over the full 373-frame time span), same dark, same sky flat, same chain, same rejection.
control: A (the incumbent) — it is the shipped model and the one the accepted products used.
hypothesis: NULL. The two displacement fields differ by 0.468 px max / 0.344 px area-weighted RMS and only 0.2 px at r=0.9 where the correction is ~12 px (887eb00). That is below the ~3.4 px in-exposure trailing floor and well below the 1.63 px centre-band effect the fitted model exists to remove (community 5.30 -> fitted 3.67 px). So both arms should land at the perpendicular-station floor with no station separating them beyond run-to-run resampling variance.
falsified_if: either arm's drift-axis CENTRE station separates from its perpendicular stations (the paraxial band signature), or seqtilt off-axis aberration differs by more than the chain's own interpolation variance. Either would mean the sub-pixel coefficient difference IS visible on a real stack and the model choice is not free.
instrument: scripts/qa/star_stations.py (findstar medians at fixed stations along/perpendicular to the solved drift axis — the band measure seqtilt is blind to) + scripts/qa/star_shape.py (Siril seqtilt: off-axis aberration, sensor tilt, truncated-mean FWHM). Judged on the tools' numbers, never on either fit's own residual.
why_it_matters: The incumbent is NOT regenerable (a re-fit under a different Hugin returns coefficients 3.9%/30.6% apart). It is now pinned as data so that does not block reproducibility — but if the re-fit is measurably equal, the repo can move to a model it can also RE-DERIVE, which is strictly more robust. If the incumbent wins, it stays and the pin is what preserves it.
verdict: NULL — CONFIRMED as hypothesized. Every one of the 9 drift-axis stations agrees within |0.02| px majFWHM (max |delta| 0.02, i.e. 0.5% of the ~3.6 px in-exposure floor), roundness within 0.007, and station counts within ~2%. seqtilt is identical on truncated-mean FWHM (3.03 vs 3.03) and differs by 0.01 px on off-axis aberration and sensor tilt — below any threshold this chain can resolve. NEITHER arm shows the paraxial band: in both, the CENTRE station (3.67 / 3.65) sits at the perpendicular-station level (3.65 / 3.64), which is the signature of a correct model; the community profile that motivated fitting read centre 5.30 against perpendicular 3.60-4.12. The 0.468 px max / 0.344 px RMS coefficient difference is real arithmetic but does NOT reach the product. CONSEQUENCE: the two models are interchangeable on this data, so the choice is free and should be made on REPRODUCIBILITY, not sharpness. The incumbent stays SHIPPED because it is what every existing product used and swapping buys nothing measurable; the x86 re-fit stays a recorded, now-MEASURED-equivalent candidate, which means a future rig that cannot install the pinned incumbent can re-derive an equivalent model from its own frames and lose nothing.

geometry.note: equal-area 700x700 station boxes, so n is directly comparable across arms despite the two arms' min-framing canvases differing slightly (4170x3385 vs 4174x3387) — the area confound the registry warns about does not apply to station counts.
